request: Dashboard history default window was derived in UTC, so a user in PST at 10pm local saw the previous UTC day. The browser contributes its IANA timezone once via a browser_tz cookie set in layouts.BaseAuth; the server computes today/yesterday in that zone (parseHistoryRange, defaultHistoryHref, buildHistoryPresets), falling back to UTC when the cookie is absent.

decisions.decision: Reused the existing branch name ft/CH6-gateway-browser-tz-cookie (no MAG-7 segment), re-cut locally off main (390fd08), instead of creating ft/CH6-MAG-7-gateway-browser-tz-cookie.
decisions.why: origin/ft/CH6-gateway-browser-tz-cookie already exists for this change and holds no commits main does not. A second branch for one change would be worse than a name missing its ticket segment; the ticket is recorded in git.ticket and every commit trailer.
CH6 was allocated when this change was first opened. The counter is monotonic and never reused; re-bumping would burn number 23 for work that already has a number.

decisions.decision: Skipped the Step 2 grill-me / performance-design interview.
decisions.why: No database object is touched, so no design gate applies, and the implementation already shipped and is under test — there is no open design choice left to grill. openspec/config.yaml's 'proposal must use grill-me' rule was satisfied when the original proposal was written.

decisions.decision: The spec delta reproduces 'Dashboard History Charts' against the TRUE current shipped behavior (RM8 start/end contract + endate-yesterday + this change's browser-TZ layer), not against the text currently in openspec/specs/gateway/spec.md.
decisions.why: The main spec is stale — it still describes the pre-RM8 ?days=N contract with default 6. A MODIFIED header replaces the whole named requirement on sync, so reproducing the stale text would have written a spec contradicting the shipped code. Consequence: archiving this change repairs the drift rather than compounding it.
